title: Google Cloud service-account key and backend .env remain in git history; rotation unrecorded
evidence: git log --all --format=%h -- aura_backend/credentials.json -> 5b37323 ("chore: add Google Cloud service account credentials file")
docs/roadmaps/AURA_CRITICAL_BACKLOG.md:99-104 (CB-06 names only the GOCSPX client secret)
current_behavior: Anyone with read access to the repository or a pre-044f417 clone can recover the service-account private key and the historical .env contents; no document records a rotation.
expected_behavior: Historical credentials rotated and the rotation recorded; history rewritten or keys provably dead.
recommendation: Rotate the service-account key(s) and every value in that .env; record the date in docs/reports/; run a one-time history secret scan as evidence; consider a history rewrite while main is still unprotected and collaborator count is low.

title: Backup container mounts the entire deploy/secrets directory (CB-08 still open)
evidence: deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml:220-284 (jwt_secret, data_encryption_keys, secrets_encryption_key, firebase_credentials.json, github_oauth_client_secret live in the same directory)
deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml:1240 (backup is on the egress network)
current_behavior: A compromise of the backup container yields every signing and encryption key, including the KEK that wraps all users' ADR-032 data keys.
expected_behavior: The backup job sees only the files it uses.
recommendation: Mount the age recipients, S3 keys and rclone.conf individually or from a ./secrets/backup/ subdirectory; add a compose fitness test asserting no service bind-mounts ./secrets wholesale.

title: On Railway the legacy per-IP rate limiter and audit source_ip see the proxy address, not the client's
evidence: aura_backend/aura_core/api/v3.py:361 and aura_core/security/rate_limit.py:202-224 (v3 limiter reads XFF itself, unaffected)
current_behavior: On the Railway target all users share one 100 req/min bucket keyed on the edge proxy address; one client can 429 the whole API and audit rows record the proxy IP.
expected_behavior: Client IP derived from the single trusted hop on every limiter and audit write.
recommendation: Set FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS (or --forwarded-allow-ips) narrowly for the Railway service, or key the legacy limiter on extract_client_ip() like v3; verify with two source IPs against production.
confidence: Medium (Railway proxy source address not observed)

title: Desktop app sign-in mints a 30-day, unscoped, unattested token that can fetch the user's data key
current_behavior: A token stolen from a desktop is a full session for a month and exposes the user's personal-OS plaintext; pairing tokens were scoped (F-09) but the app's own login was not.
expected_behavior: Desktop app sessions short-lived and refreshable (device-bound refresh), or scoped away from /keys/data and admin routes.
recommendation: Issue the desktop app a 15-minute access + device-bound refresh pair; keep the 30-day form for the scoped daemon only; document the interim trade in ADR-032.

title: Production CORS default includes localhost origins with credentials (SEC-12 still open)
current_behavior: A page on a developer's localhost can make credentialed cross-origin calls to production; impact bounded because the API is bearer-only.
expected_behavior: Production default names only production origins.
recommendation: Drop localhost from the prod default; set ALLOWED_ORIGINS explicitly on Railway.

title: fetch_url reads the whole response body into memory before truncating
current_behavior: A multi-GB allowlisted URL is fully buffered before the 20,000-char cap; DNS-rebinding TOCTOU acknowledged in code.
recommendation: Use client.stream() and abort past a byte budget (e.g. 1 MB); keep the char cap.

title: Audit log and turn telemetry hold email and source IP with no retention and survive erasure
evidence: grep for purge/retention over aura_audit_events and aura_turn_telemetry: none
current_behavior: After erasure the subject's email and IPs persist indefinitely in audit rows; telemetry likewise.
expected_behavior: Documented retention enforced by a periodic purge; erasure pseudonymises the subject's actor field.
recommendation: Celery beat purge with configurable days; on erasure replace actor with a hash; state the policy in docs/.

title: Session/device revocation scans all Redis keys; no refresh-token reuse detection
current_behavior: O(total sessions) Redis round trips per demotion or erasure; a replayed consumed refresh token is refused without revoking its family.
expected_behavior: Per-uid index sets; family revocation on replay.
recommendation: Write uid-indexed sets at issue time; revoke the family when a consumed token is replayed.

title: Documents and chunks stored in plaintext in Postgres and Qdrant payloads; third-party Qdrant on Railway
current_behavior: Uploaded document text is readable by anyone with DB or Qdrant access and leaves the control plane on the Railway target.
expected_behavior: An explicit decision per target on document confidentiality; optionally sealed chunk text.
recommendation: Record the decision in the ADR owning the Railway split; if confidentiality is wanted, seal aura_chunks.content and Qdrant text payloads with the owner's DEK.

title: VPS gateway trusts X-Forwarded-For from any container (--forwarded-allow-ips='*')
current_behavior: Any container on the gateway's networks can spoof client IP to the limiters and audit.
recommendation: Replace '*' with the nginx service address or edge subnet in both compose files.

title: hostd control-server token file permissions not restricted (SEC-01 residual)
evidence: grep 0600|chmod|umask|writeAsString in aura_hostd/lib/src/control_server.dart: no permission handling (doc comment at :13 only)
current_behavior: control.json, holding the bearer that can flip workspace trust, is written with the process umask.
recommendation: Write to a temp file, restrict permissions, then rename.

title: No command_timeout on the asyncpg pool; legacy SQLAlchemy engine never disposed; connection budget uncomputed
current_behavior: A slow statement holds a pool slot indefinitely; two pools per worker across gateway and Celery workers can exceed Postgres's default 100 connections.
expected_behavior: Per-statement timeout and a documented, enforced connection budget.
recommendation: Pass command_timeout and max_inactive_connection_lifetime to create_pool; compute the budget per deployment and set max_connections explicitly.

title: Legacy plaintext rows are read silently after keys are configured
evidence: aura_backend/scripts/reencrypt_fields.py (exists; no evidence it ran on Railway)
current_behavior: Rows written before AURA_DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEYS was set stay plaintext and are indistinguishable from outside.
expected_behavior: A count of remaining plaintext rows is visible and driven to zero.
recommendation: Expose a needs_reencryption counter via metrics/readiness, run the script, record the output.
